fact_text: In the Islamic banking model, the bank invests depositors' funds and profits are shared, rather than depositors receiving a fixed interest rate.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: In mudaraba the investor supplies capital while a manager runs the business and makes decisions, and both share profit; musharaka is a joint-capital partnership that also shares profit.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Conventional lending was said to often rest on paper assets, while Shariah-compliant financing is asset-backed, tied to a real asset that has intrinsic value.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Riba is a loan on which the lender adds an increment agreed in advance, such as 5% or 10%; the interviewee said this definition has been consistent across Muslim jurisprudence and history.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The riba rule applies to goods as well as money: lending a tonne of rice and getting 10% more back is riba, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Islamic banks avoid lending at interest by one of three routes: trade (sale and purchase), profit-and-loss participation, or asset-backed leasing and rent.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Ijara is asset leasing in which the bank owns the asset, rents it to the customer and earns rent instead of interest.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Non-consumable real assets such as buildings, cars and laptops can be rented under this rule because they are used for years without being consumed, whereas consumables like rice cannot carry a premium.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: In the Islamic home-finance example given, the customer funds 20% and the bank owns 80% of the house, and the customer rents the bank's share instead of taking an interest-bearing mortgage.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: In murabaha trade financing the bank buys goods a client needs, holds them briefly and resells them to the client with a disclosed margin added.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: A conventional bank lends money and earns the extra amount as interest, while an Islamic bank says it charges a profit or markup on a financed asset rather than interest.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: A commercial Islamic bank cannot offer interest-free qard hasan loans, which are repaid only at principal, so it must earn depositor and shareholder returns through trade, leasing or profit-sharing.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Meezan Bank's linked Ehsan Trust provides qard hasan, interest-free loans repaid at principal, including education loans for students, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Meezan Bank was founded as an Islamic bank rather than converted from a conventional model, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Faysal Bank was cited as a large conventional bank that converted into an Islamic bank, one of the major conversions the interviewee described.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Many conventional banks in Pakistan already run Islamic windows, which the interviewee said shows the wider system is still in transition.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The State Bank's core role is financial-system stability, and the government has added a mandate for it to steer the financial system toward Shariah compliance, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The government set a target for the whole financial system to be fully Shariah-compliant by 2028, and the interviewee said the change needed across the economy is far bigger than banking alone.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The State Bank's Islamic banking division grew in size and regulatory weight over about 30 years as large banks converted to Islamic operations, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The Banking Companies Ordinance has a chapter on Islamic banking, and the interviewee read it as letting Islamic banks trade goods where the trade supports financing.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Conventional banking took about 300 years to evolve, and the interviewee said Islamic banking will also refine its rules over time as the sector develops.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The main barrier to full Islamic conversion, the interviewee said, is finding enough suitable assets to invest in and managing liquidity, which sukuk market development is meant to address.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The interviewee argued that a firm national deadline is needed to keep conversion serious, and that the main obstacle is mindset and culture rather than technical capacity.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The State Bank's team and an Islamic banks committee are pushing the conversion agenda with the Finance Ministry, and academic centres are needed to widen research, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The interviewee sits on the State Bank's Shariah Advisory Committee, where obstacles to converting the financial system are discussed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Islamic banking drew liquidity from depositors who had avoided interest-based banking, boosting both current and savings deposits, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Islamic banks deploy only about half of the liquidity they aim to place, the interviewee said, because Shariah-compliant placement options are limited.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Government sukuk and PIBs are available to conventional banks at close to double their liquidity, the interviewee said, giving conventional banks far more placement room than Islamic banks.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The government pays higher returns on PIBs than on sukuk, the interviewee said, because Islamic banks accept lower returns on sukuk, a pattern seen across the economy.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Islamic banks pay depositors lower profit partly because deposit liquidity has grown faster than the number of Shariah-compliant placements, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Financial penetration in Muslim countries, including Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, was low partly because riba concerns kept many people out of banking, the interviewee said, citing an earlier multi-country study.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Islamic home-finance is the most in-demand Islamic banking product, because customers otherwise pay rent indefinitely or take a conventional mortgage, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Some non-Muslim customers also seek interest-free products, and Islamic banks have a large presence in London with growing presence elsewhere, the interviewee said.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: Islamic banks often call their charge profit or markup rather than interest; the interviewee said the label differs but the mechanism of charging for money is the same.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The finance expert argued that a PKR 100 or PKR 1,000 note has no intrinsic utility of its own, so money cannot be charged for beyond its face value.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)

fact_text: The guest said a PKR 100 loan may be repaid only as PKR 100, not PKR 110, because charging extra on a loan is prohibited in Islamic finance.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'The Biggest Myths About Islamic Banking Explained by a Finance Expert | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-03-13)
